research.title: Meta Blueprint: Increase campaign performance with diversified creative
research.note: Primary guidance to diversify by concept, motivator, and format. Does not establish a winner for any individual photo.

concepts.title: A face worth framing
concepts.angle: A portrait as something worth keeping
concepts.brief: A stark contemporary art-gallery invitation: warm ivory cotton paper, just one confident vermilion dry-brush sweep along the extreme lower left edge and a fine deep-brown irregular ink line along the far right edge. Subtle tactile print grain, lots of calm blank paper. Sophisticated independent photographic zine energy, beautifully minimal. No outlined rectangle, central frame, gold, metallic foil, leaves, branches, botanical elements, ornamental flourishes, wedding stationery, cream-on-cream torn-paper layers or bohemian decoration.
concepts.background_prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing. Create ONE original graphic BACKGROUND ART PLATE for a vertical 9:16 portrait-photography invitation. This is only the abstract paper-and-ink design layer; actual photographs and readable type will be composited separately with deterministic layout. Absolutely NO photographs, people, human figures, faces, letters, words, numbers, logos, watermark, app interface, fake controls, or typography of any kind.
Composition must be flat graphic art filling the entire canvas, not a photograph of a poster in a room. Preserve a generous relatively calm TOP BAND (y=8% to 29%) for two large headline lines; a generous clean CENTRAL RECTANGULAR SPACE (x=9% to 91%, y=33% to 78%) for one portrait; a calm LOWER BAND (y=80% to 91%) for a small profile-photo bubble and invitation. Decoration should primarily live in the outer 8% of the canvas, so the original portrait will remain the focal point. Don't draw a placeholder icon or a human silhouette. Every blank zone should be the same attractive background paper; no checkerboard or transparency. Original, confidently art-directed, tactile materials, controlled shapes and strong color, polished independent editorial design.  Never draw an outlined rectangle or a visible central frame; the portrait frame will be added in code.
